question.text: If futures trade at fair value (F = S + C), an arbitrageur will:

answer.text: Not trade, as there is no arbitrage opportunity
Buy spot and sell futures for a guaranteed profit
Sell spot and buy futures for a guaranteed profit
Trade in the options market instead

explanation.text: The Logic: Per workbook p.52, the buyer is indifferent when the futures-spot difference exactly matches cost of carry, so at fair value (F = S + C) there is no arbitrage. A buy-spot/sell-futures trade would only cover carrying costs with no net profit. The Trap: At fair value, buying spot and selling futures nets exactly zero after accounting for carrying costs. Per workbook pp.102-103, spot-versus-futures arbitrage exists only when fair price differs from the traded futures price. Note: An arbitrage opportunity arises only when the traded futures price diverges from the fair (cost-of-carry) value.
